sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Vivek Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1.

Heard Sri Lavkush Kumar Bhatt, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Ranvijay, Advocate
holding brief of Sri Vivek Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 and learned A.G.A.
for the State.

2.  The instant petition has been preferred for challenging the order dated 16.02.2023 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate, Sadar, Farrukhabad in Case No.448 of 2023 (State vs. Dhirendra and Others), through which cognizance of offence under sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. has been taken up against the petitioners as well as to set-aside the order dated 16.07.2024 passed by learned revisional court, through which order dated 16.02.2023 has been upheld.
Virendra Kumar Dixit And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195238266/
1 3.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the story developed by the informant-respondent no.2 appears to be false and malicious, therefore the impugned orders dated 16.02.2023 and 16.07.2024 passed by learned concerned courts are totally illegal, arbitrary and against the material available on record and as such the above proceedings initiated against the petitioners may be set-aside.
4.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for respondent no.2 rebutted the stand taken up by learned counsel for the petitioners and submitted that from perusal of material available on record as well as the impugned orders, it is crystal clear that the proceedings initiated against the petitioners are correct and learned court below had applied his judicial mind and rightly taken up cognizance of offence against the petitioners and the petitioners are only trying to avoid the appearance before the court concerned.
5. From the perusal of the material on record and looking into the facts of the case, at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the petitioners.

6. Accordingly, I find no infirmity and perversity in the impugned orders passed by learned concerned courts and as such, this petition stands dismissed.
Order Date :- 8.11.2024
